thread:
incident-bot: Paging: p99 latency spike & streaming stalls observed in dedicated-us-west-2 pool (model: gptx-8q). Auto-escalation to on-call. Alert: p99 > 2.5s for 5m, streaming stalls detected on ~15% of in-flight streams. Dash: https://redwood.internal/dash/pools/us-west-2

sarah_oncall: On it. I'm oncall for infra — hitting the incident playbook. First triage: scope of impacted customers? any 502/503 errors?

luis_support: Seeing multiple customers report degraded stream responsiveness and occasional aborted streams (client logs show "stream closed by server"). No mass 502s but a handful of 504s tied to long tail. I can DM affected account IDs.

matt_eng-runtime: Telemetry: queue depth for dedicated-us-west-2 hotshot pool jumped from 40 -> 280 in ~3m. Autoscaler attempted to provision new slots but warmup handshake times are ~18s which is longer than usual (target ~6s). Handshake logs: `handshake: slot_assign timeout=18000ms`

jane_sre: +1 on queue depth. KV-cache cold-path hit rate increased from 2% -> 48% for that pool, so model warmup cost per slot is higher. Are these newly created pools or customers bursting?

luis_support: Most spikes line up with customer A and a couple of batch ingestion jobs from customer B kicked off around the same time. Looks like burst + cold-cache amplification.

sarah_oncall: Mitigation options: 1) failover streaming to compatible model variant in other region 2) force-scale up dedicated pool (manual) 3) enable short-term queue shedding for lower-tier customers. Thoughts?

matt_eng-runtime: Quick wins: force-scale up + warmup parallelization. I can manually add 8 slots to hotshot pool now; however new slots will still incur warmup. We can also enable prefix/KV cache priming for gptx-8q which should reduce per-slot warmup cost — need platform permission.

incident-bot: deploy-bot initiated: deploy request #d-9321 to add 8-hotshot-slots to dedicated-us-west-2 accepted by platform but will run preflight checks (ETA ~45s).

jane_sre: While we wait, recommend enabling routing fallback rule: route streaming requests for the affected customer IDs to dedicated-us-west-2-fallback (quantized variant gptx-8q-4q) in a canary mode (10% traffic) to verify stream stability. Fallback avoids heavy warmup but might slightly change latency/quality.

kayla_cs: Customer success: If we route a subset to fallback variant, I'll prep messaging to Customer A so they're aware of slight quality tradeoffs. They prefer availability over small quality diffs.

matt_eng-runtime: Command to prime caches (internal):
```
# prime kv cache for model on pool
redwoodctl prime-cache --pool dedicated-us-west-2 --model gptx-8q --prefix 0xabc123 --concurrency 4
```
I'll run with concurrency 4. Expect ~6s per slot improvement after priming.

sarah_oncall: Go for it. Also enable queue shedding: drop requests with route tag `low-tier` when queue depth > 200. Jane, can you push that throttle rule?

jane_sre: Pushing rule now: `route/throttle/dedicated-us-west-2` set to drop `low-tier` when queue_depth >= 200. Pushed and active.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: manual-scale job d-9321 now started. Estimated worker ready in ~22s.

matt_eng-runtime: priming started. Logs: `prime: started 8 workers` `prime: per-slot warmup reduced from 18s -> ~7s for primed slots`

luis_support: Customer A reports improved smoothness on the canary route for those 10% sessions — no aborted streams. Kayla: will update account channel.

sarah_oncall: Monitoring: p99 now dropping from 2.8s -> 1.1s across 5m window. Streaming stall rate down from 15% -> 3%. Queue depth trending down to 120. Good signs.

jane_sre: Follow-up actions: 1) postmortem root-cause: warmup amplification due to KV-cache cold-path + bursty customer traffic + autoscaler handshake timeout. 2) short term: increase warmup parallelism and reduce handshake timeout back to 6s after patch. 3) medium term: pre-warm heuristics for customers that historically burst, and adjust autoscaler to pre-allocate buffer headroom.

kayla_cs: Noted. I'll coordinate customer comms (FYI + RCA after postmortem).

incident-bot: Reminder: paging window extended 30m for oncall. Next oncall rotation: matt_eng-runtime will takeover at 4270012399. Sarah please handoff any outstanding ops.

sarah_oncall: Handing off live watch to matt_eng-runtime. Outstanding: keep the throttle rule for 1h, verify autoscaler handshake fixes in next deploy, and capture any further anomalies to the incident timeline. I'm available as backup.

matt_eng-runtime: Acknowledged. I'll keep an eye and follow up with an ops runbook tweak to avoid similar handshake delays. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: job d-9321 reported: 8 slots ready. All healthchecks passed.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: severity: high, impact: degraded streaming and elevated p99 tail for dedicated-us-west-2; mitigation: manual-scale + cache priming + route throttle + fallback canary; status: mitigated -> monitoring.

jane_sre: Filing the postmortem and linking timeline + logs: https://redwood.internal/pm/4270012345. Assigning action items: warmup-heuristics (matt), autoscaler-timeouts (infra team), prewarm-list (customer-success).

luis_support: I'll collect affected session logs and customer tickets and attach them to the PM.

sarah_oncall: Closing live paging. If p99 creeps back up, reopen immediately.

matt_eng-runtime: Closing shift — will pick up monitoring.
